title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 75
paragraphs: There was another distinguished deed done by Sophanes: when the Athenians were besieging Aegina, he challenged to a fight and killed Eurybates the Argive, who had been victor in the pentathlon at the games. To Sophanes himself it happened, after these events, that while he was general of the Athenians together with Leagros son of Glaucon, he was killed — after proving himself a good man — by the Edonians at Daton, fighting for the gold mines.
